  display: block;
  position: absolute;
  width: 40px;

  margin: 8px;
  border: 2px solid var(--primary-color);
  border-radius: 50%;
  animation: styles_idsLoading__1gVYZ 1.2s cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.5, 1) infinite;
  border-color: var(--primary-color) transparent transparent transparent;
}
.styles_idsLoading__1gVYZ div:nth-child(1) {
  animation-delay: -0.45s;
}
.styles_idsLoading__1gVYZ div:nth-child(2) {
  animation-delay: -0.3s;
}
.styles_idsLoading__1gVYZ div:nth-child(3) {
  animation-delay: -0.15s;
}

<strong>Northern Ireland goal</strong>: Kelly (64)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">Michael Olise continued to stake his claim as one of the world's best footballers with his first career hat-trick. The winger opened the scoring against Northern Ireland with a tap in after Ousmane Dembele saw his effort blocked. He then doubled his money after the break with an unerring finish from the top of the box. <strong>Uzbekistan goal</strong>: Sergeev (90+2)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">Cody Gakpo scored twice from the penalty spot to help a 10-man Netherlands overcome Fabio Cannavaro's Uzbekistan. Tunisia hit the post three times in the first 45 minutes, the last coming from an Anis Slimane free kick after Laimer was sent off for a handball. Austria hung tough and Marcel Sabitzer delivered the winner when he knifed into the area and steered home a right-footed finish.</p><div class="ff-mb-32 article-section_images__7k4ik"><div class="row"><div class="col-12 d-flex justify-content-center"><picture class="ff-text-blue-dark text-xs text-regular ff-mb-0" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto;"><img src="https://digitalhub.fifa.com/transform/c31508fa-11ef-4575-9eae-3c2894bf47e9/Marcel-Sabitzer-celebrates-with-Austria-teammates?focuspoint=0.48,0.29&io=transform:fill,width:768&quality=75" srcset="https://digitalhub.fifa.com/transform/c31508fa-11ef-4575-9eae-3c2894bf47e9/Marcel-Sabitzer-celebrates-with-Austria-teammates?focuspoint=0.48,0.29&io=transform:fill,width:640&quality=75 640w, https://digitalhub.fifa.com/transform/c31508fa-11ef-4575-9eae-3c2894bf47e9/Marcel-Sabitzer-celebrates-with-Austria-teammates?focuspoint=0.48,0.29&io=transform:fill,width:768&quality=75 768w, https://digitalhub.fifa.com/transform/c31508fa-11ef-4575-9eae-3c2894bf47e9/Marcel-Sabitzer-celebrates-with-Austria-teammates?focuspoint=0.48,0.29&io=transform:fill,width:1024&quality=75 1024w, https://digitalhub.fifa.com/transform/c31508fa-11ef-4575-9eae-3c2894bf47e9/Marcel-Sabitzer-celebrates-with-Austria-teammates?focuspoint=0.48,0.29&io=transform:fill,width:1366&quality=75 1366w, " sizes="(min-width: 1440px) 50vw, (min-width: 1024px) 70vw, 100vw" alt="Austria's forward #09 Marcel Sabitzer (2nd L) celebrates scoring the opening goal with his teammates during the friendly football match between Austria and Tunisia in Vienna, Austria on June 1, 2026 ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup football tournament. (Photo by Joe Klamar / AFP via Getty Images)" style="display: block; max-width: 100%; height: auto;"></picture></div></div></div><hr class="rich-text_hr__2C63+ article-section_articleHr__BchCk"><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Norway 3-1 Sweden " style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/3opvxhr7pjj488919ntvlsaok">Norway 3-1 Sweden </a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Norway 3-1 Sweden " style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/3opvxhr7pjj488919ntvlsaok">Norway 3-1 Sweden </a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Norway goals:</strong> Jorgen Strand Larsen (8, 33), Antonio Nusa (18)
<strong>Sweden goal: </strong>Alexander Isak (76)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">In the battle of the two Scandinavian teams at the World Cup, Norway emerged triumphant in Oslo. What was all the more impressive was that it came without the rested superstars Martin Odegaard and Erling Haaland. Jorgen Strand Larsen found the net twice in the first half with his head, with Antonio Nusa also blasting home a thunderous strike. In a much-improved display after the break, Alexander Isak pulled a goal back for Sweden with a brilliant individual effort.</p><hr class="rich-text_hr__2C63+ article-section_articleHr__BchCk"><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Türkiye 4-0 North Macedonia " style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/d1ptnx1dkhecu0ahm9c515jbo">Türkiye 4-0 North Macedonia </a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Türkiye 4-0 North Macedonia " style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/d1ptnx1dkhecu0ahm9c515jbo">Türkiye 4-0 North Macedonia </a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Türkiye goals:</strong> Orkun Kokcu (2), Can Uzun (16), Deniz Gul (52), Baris Alper Yilmaz (70)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">Türkiye continued to build momentum for the global showpiece with a comfortable victory over North Macedonia in Istanbul. Vincenzo Montella's men showed their intent from the opening whistle when they hit the crossbar after just ten seconds and Orkun Kokcu struck home with 61 seconds on the clock. A comfortable victory was sealed by Can Uzun's near-post strike followed by second-half efforts from Deniz Gul and Baris Alper Yilmaz. Star man Arda Guler showed some neat touches in making a second-half cameo.</p><hr class="rich-text_hr__2C63+ article-section_articleHr__BchCk"><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title=""31 May"" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><strong>31 May</strong></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title=""31 May"" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><strong>31 May</strong></span></span></h3><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Brazil 6-2 Panama" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/6ldgjtk9kf1tcfyppin95dxxw">Brazil 6-2 Panama</a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Brazil 6-2 Panama" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/6ldgjtk9kf1tcfyppin95dxxw">Brazil 6-2 Panama</a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Brazil goals: </strong>Vinicius Junior (2), Casemiro (39), Rayan (53), Lucas Paqueta (60) Igor Thiago (63 pen), Danilo (81)<strong>
Panama goals: </strong>Matheus Cunha own goal (14), Carlos Harvey (84)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">Carlo Ancelotti's Brazil hit six of the best to steamroll Panama in Rio de Janeiro. Vinicius Junior opened the scoring with a rasping long-range drive, but Brazil were pegged back when Amir Murillo's free-kick deflected in off Matheus Cunha. Casemiro reestablished the <em>Seleção's</em> lead shortly before the break by flicking in a Vinicius shot. Rayan then netted his first for Brazil, with Lucas Paqueta, Igor Thiago and Danilo adding further gloss. The evening ended on a high for Panama, as Carlos Harvey netted with a fizzing first-time shot.</p><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="USA 3-2 Senegal" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/26e8v0cri9vyp6f8uhqdn2yhg">USA 3-2 Senegal</a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="USA 3-2 Senegal" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/26e8v0cri9vyp6f8uhqdn2yhg">USA 3-2 Senegal</a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>USA goals: </strong>Sergino Dest (7), Christian Pulisic (20), Folarin Balogun (63)<strong>
Senegal goals: </strong>Sadio Mane (44, 52)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">Co-hosts USA edged a topsy-turvy game with Senegal in Charlotte. Goals from Sergino Dest and captain Christian Pulisic saw the States race into a two-goal lead, but the match was flipped on its head either side of the break. Senegal captain Sadio Mane was sent through to finish an incisive counter-attack, before capitalising on a mix-up in the USA rearguard to level the contest. Mauricio Pochettino's men wouldn't be denied, however, with Folarin Balogun slotting home from a low Tim Weah cross.</p><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Germany 4-0 Finland" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/39uvapacloh2rntjoyixww55g">Germany 4-0 Finland</a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Germany 4-0 Finland" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/39uvapacloh2rntjoyixww55g">Germany 4-0 Finland</a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Germany goals: </strong>Deniz Undav (34, 57), Florian Wirtz (48), Jamal Musiala (63)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">Deniz Undav scored two and made another as Germany cruised to victory in their penultimate World Cup warm-up match. The Stuttgart striker headed in the opener following a well-worked corner, before turning provider for Florian Wirtz to double the lead. Undav completed his brace just before the hour mark, while Jamal Musiala's first Germany goal in over a year added the gloss to a clinical second-half display.</p><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Cabo Verde 3-0 Serbia" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/c4pq3e6ss6258jq1d6xodj6s4">Cabo Verde 3-0 Serbia</a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Cabo Verde 3-0 Serbia" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/c4pq3e6ss6258jq1d6xodj6s4">Cabo Verde 3-0 Serbia</a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Cabo Verde goals: </strong>Kevin Lenini (11), Laros Duarte (59), Gilson Benchimol (63)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">Cabo Verde claimed back-to-back wins over European opposition for the first time since 2022 with a dominant victory over Serbia. They defeated Finland 2-1 back in March, and were set on their way in Lisbon thanks to Kevin Lenini. Laros Duarte then doubled their lead with a well-worked goal following a one-two with Steven Moreira, before Gilson Benchimol slammed a third home to make the game safe.</p><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Czechia 2-1 Kosovo" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/635l3kmice8cnwq53ligaupec">Czechia 2-1 Kosovo</a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Czechia 2-1 Kosovo" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/635l3kmice8cnwq53ligaupec">Czechia 2-1 Kosovo</a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Czechia goals: </strong>Tomas Ladra (11), Adam Hlozek (31)<strong>
Kosovo goal: </strong>Lindon Emerllahu (79)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">A fine display from Adam Hlozek helped Czechia to victory in this all-European affair. The powerful forward burst away from a host of Kosovan defenders to set up David Doudera, who in turn crossed for Tomas Landra to head in from inside the six-yard box. Hlozek then scored the second himself, firing home a pass from Mojmir Chytil. Lindon Emerllahu halved the deficit with a close-range effort late in the piece, but Czechia held on to go five games unbeaten.</p><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Switzerland 4-1 Jordan" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/33t6y7jo2iyut9egdjk9jpd78">Switzerland 4-1 Jordan</a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Switzerland 4-1 Jordan" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/33t6y7jo2iyut9egdjk9jpd78">Switzerland 4-1 Jordan</a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Switzerland goals:</strong> Breel Embolo (28 pen), Dan Ndoye (33), Granit Xhaka (45+9 pen), Christian Fassnacht (79)
<strong>Jordan goal:</strong> Odeh Fakhoury (52)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">A dominant first-half display saw Switzerland down fellow World Cup 2026 side Jordan in St. Gallen. Breel Embolo got the <em>Nati</em> up and running with a first-half penalty, before Dan Ndoye was set clear by Michel Aebischer to slot a second soon after. Captain Granit Xhaka then extended the lead in first-half stoppage time from the spot. Substitute Odeh Fakhoury looked to have given Jordan a lifeline with a well-placed shot shortly after the break, but all hopes of a comeback were extinguished when Christian Fassnacht finished well from the centre of the box.</p><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Japan 1-0 Iceland" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/42fafb27a9cce9p9qzjepfro">Japan 1-0 Iceland</a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Japan 1-0 Iceland" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/42fafb27a9cce9p9qzjepfro">Japan 1-0 Iceland</a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Japan goal: </strong>Koki Ogawa (87)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">The game was marked by a poignant early moment, as defender Maya Yoshida was replaced to a standing ovation after 14 minutes in what was the 37-year-old's 127th and final appearance. Japan settled down from then and enjoyed the better of the chances throughout, eventually breaking the deadlock when Koki Ogawa glanced home a Yukinari Sugawara cross from the right to secure Japan a sixth consecutive victory.</p><hr class="rich-text_hr__2C63+ article-section_articleHr__BchCk"><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title=""30 May "" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><strong>30 May </strong></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title=""30 May "" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><strong>30 May </strong></span></span></h3><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Mexico 1-0 Australia " style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/arj1vbjk2e4c53nfz7i0i3mdw">Mexico 1-0 Australia </a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Mexico 1-0 Australia " style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/arj1vbjk2e4c53nfz7i0i3mdw">Mexico 1-0 Australia </a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Mexico goal:</strong> Johan Vasquez (28)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">At a heaving, and decidedly pro-Mexico, Rose Bowl, Javier Aguirre handed several fringe players a final chance to impress while there was no Cristian Volpato for the Socceroos, after he recently switched his international allegiance from Italy. In a clash that El Tri dominated, Johan Vasquez’s first-half header ultimately proved the difference. </p><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Scotland 4-1 Curaçao" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/2m7tx0pz7j6s4e7y4gycck8wk">Scotland 4-1 Curaçao</a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Scotland 4-1 Curaçao" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/2m7tx0pz7j6s4e7y4gycck8wk">Scotland 4-1 Curaçao</a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Scotland goals:</strong> Lawrence Shankland (59, 64), Findlay Curtis (45), Ryan Christie (81 pen)
<strong>Curaçao goal:</strong> Tahith Chong (17)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">Steve Clarke's Scots came from a goal down to earn a resounding win over ten-man Curaçao in Glasgow. A Lawrence Shankland double, sandwiched in between a smart finish from teenager Findlay Curtis and a Ryan Christie penalty, sent the Hampden crowd home happy after Tahith Chong had opened the scoring with a superb solo goal. The game turned on a first-half red card for Juergen Locadia, spoiling Dick Advocaat's return to the country he spent three years in as Rangers manager.</p><h3 class="ff-text-blue-dark article-section_headings__iQUD7"><span class="d-md-none"><span title="Ecuador 2-1 Saudi Arabia" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/2pdq43eo947vum679tj81q3o4">Ecuador 2-1 Saudi Arabia</a></span></span><span class="d-none d-md-block"><span title="Ecuador 2-1 Saudi Arabia" style="display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;"><a href="https://www.fifa.com/en/match-centre/match/cesdwwnxbc5fmajgroc0hqzy2/dezv8l0fzgcxtejl0dwmy1gyc/2m1wojm5bt709wu4kugtytxqs/2pdq43eo947vum679tj81q3o4">Ecuador 2-1 Saudi Arabia</a></span></span></h3><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular"><strong>Ecuador goals: </strong>Jackson Porozo (39), Anthony Valencia (51)
<strong>Saudi Arabia goal:</strong> Sultan Mandash (87)</p><p class="rich-text_p__UfX5b article-section_articleParagraph__pYCnd text-regular">Ecuador kicked off their preparation with a narrow victory over Saudi Arabia at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, New Jersey. The South Americans struck when John Yeboah served up a free kick and Jackson Porozo met it with a header into net. Yeboah then played provider again, this time setting up Anthony Valencia's finish to double the lead.
